[b]Grievance of Petitions[/b]

[i]In unanimous consent under the authority of the first conference of the true international association for Rosenmarkket-Montfleurois union, signed in the presence of three witnesses[/i] we do hold that when a time comes for a people to take upon themselves the burden of liberty, and raise their heads to the peaks of prosperity, seeking for themselves harmony from a government of oppression and by God, liberating themselves from the chains of sorrow. 

We hold that this time has come now upon the good people of Rosenmarkke, who have for years been oppressed in increasing means and manners, to secede from the Republic of Rosenmarkke to secure for themselves the inalienable rights endowed upon them by their creator, chief among these the right to life and liberty. And that to secure these rights, the sacred bands of the state, having been degraded by the state itself through various means and manners by which it did so, the bands shall be broken. 

It is in this manner that we present this petition of secession and of grievances to the world and to the government of Rosenmarkke, whereas:

The government of Rosenmarkke has failed in its duty to maintain the basic right to life, through endless wars and tyranny, which have killed and led many to be killed. 

The government of Rosenmarkke has violated its own promises of freedom, obstructing and burdening the people with unlawful decrees and acts curtailing their speech, their religion, and their movements.

The government of Rosenmarkke has resorted to the use of force against the dissidents of the regime, seeking to silence the alternative voices that would restore justice and peace to all people.

The government of Rosenmarkke has stripped the workers of their right to choice and fair wage bargaining through the laws and decrees of Polenne Strømm, burdening the workers under the mandate of the state.

The government of Rosenmarkke has waged unlawful warfare against foreign powers, and thereby upon its own people, as these powers have inflicted damage and retribution upon the state.

The government of Rosenmarkke has sought to spy out and, with great speed, eliminate the pockets of dissent through the usage of state networks contrary to international law, resolving and resorting to the use of torture and secret arrests. 

These being the chief violations of the state of Rosenmarkke for the reason by which we write and sign this petition before the eyes of the world, we therefore call for the immediate redress of grievances and the full and formal reunification of all regions to the Montfleurois state as deemed by history to be the rightful state of the region.

Signed this day, July 5, 2028

[quote=lyuongo;61594020][i][b]Even with[/b][/i] the new developments of Aoka and Basadihsthani support, Thet Mg knew Uria only had a day or so at most to hold out for. The Navy had defected, and even if Mg could contact his LNA allies in the south, there would be no way of getting around the LNSA stronghold now splattered across western Lyuongo. Mg looked over the cheap board laid out in front of him. There were a lot more chocolates now on the ground then on the board. At this, Thet turned to look out the window, where he was met with a sea of rubble, broken up by the occasional fire. Shutting the blinds, Mg marched over to the other side of the room, feet kicking up dirt and bits and pieces of the concrete roof above that had cracked in the LNSA bombing raids. On a wooden shelf, Mg picked up his silver revolver, to which he inspected it. "This may be the last bit of still shiny metal in this entire city..." he thought, before setting it back down. Mg walked back over to the table, ripped the map off of the table, kicked the table over, grabbed his rifle and left for the ever-shrinking front. 

From a third person's perspective, the front was now a perimeter with a radius of about 360 yards around Mg's makeshift HQ. The few tanks they did have were now reduced to a pile of scrap metal. Not like they were much of anything before being blown up... anyways, eventually Uria did fall. 4th of June, the year of our Lord two-thousand and twenty eight at fifteen-hundred hours and thirty-eight minutes was when the last LNA defender of Uria fell to the LNSA onslaught, announced by the LNSA. This marked the end of the first stage of the Lyuongoan Civil War, with both sides now split between the east and west of the great Lyuongoan Jungle. Tung Aung, now with an international coalition at his back, is being pressured by the mining companies to start an offensive in the north. However, President Tung wanted to stall until the Aoka Air Force could gain air dominance over Lyuongo. Deciding to straddle both lines, Tung ordered a bombing run of about 10 MiGs to take off from an air base in the city of Durgo to strafe Yapinaw, an admittably half-assed measure.

The National Salvation Army would be halted for several days as they attempted to beat the cyberattacks, though the general digital incompetence meant they gave up, it wasted several days before Hein decided to simply begin transmitting messages via motorcycle. Several hundred would die to the half-assed bombing Republican runs - perhaps due to a miracle.

Hein would order whatever aircraft not bombed out to follow the convoy going to Yapinau, to bomb Durgo and any positions spotted from the sky, though it would largely be ineffective with the lack of communication, still, a bombed city is a bombed city!
